And Saladin replied:
"These countries were not yours originally, but belonged to the Greeks.
And the Arabs, at the beginning of their going forth,
took them away from the Greeks.
And when the Arabs became somewhat weak,
you came and took them from them.
And we now have turned and taken our countries from you.
And regarding Jerusalem, of which you say that it is our house of worship,
it is also our house of worship as well.
And more than you, we magnify it and honor it,
just as God has commanded us in His Quran."
And again the King of England sent to Saladin, saying:
"I wish that your brother al-Malik al-Adil should become my brother-in-law by [marrying] my sister, who has come with me to worship in Jerusalem.
Therefore, if you give the cities of the seacoast to your brother,
so that he may rule over the fortresses and cities alone,
and that all the villages belong to the Templars and Hospitallers,
this marriage shall take place.
And I also will give to my sister all the cities of the seacoast that are in the hands of the Franks,
and my sister's residence shall be in Jerusalem."
Saladin, however, would not agree to this either.
But Adil, his brother, burned with desire,
and he sent nobles and elders to his brother Saladin to make him consent.
And while he was strongly objecting,
those shrewd men said to him:
"We know that this will never happen,
nor does that woman, the daughter of a great king, desire to belong to an Arab.
And her brother also knows this full well,
and it is possible that by way of mockery, as he is accustomed to jest,
in his cunning he sent and told us these things;
therefore do not grieve your brother."
And thus Saladin was persuaded,
and he sent an envoy of agreement to the king.
And when he had detained the envoy for three days with him,
on the third day he said to him:
"Behold, during these three days, night and day, I have been persuading my sister, but she is not persuaded.
And she says:
'If he becomes a true Christian,
this shall be,
and if not, no.'"
And thus the envoy of Saladin returned, being put to shame.
And in those days Taqi al-Din Umar, the nephew of Saladin, died on the road to Khilat, as he was going to make war against it;
and they brought him back and buried him in Mayperqat [Martyropolis].
